Summarize this article: The local council announced a new initiative on Tuesday aimed at reducing traffic
congestion in the city center. The plan includes expanding bus routes, adding
protected bike lanes on three major streets, and introducing a congestion charge
for vehicles entering downtown during peak hours starting next spring. Officials
said the changes were driven by a study showing that average commute times had
increased by 22% over the past five years, with downtown air quality also
declining. Business owners in the area expressed mixed reactions: some welcomed
the reduced congestion as good for foot traffic, while others worried the
congestion charge would discourage customers from driving in. The council plans
to hold public consultations over the next two months before finalizing the
policy, with a final vote expected in early autumn.
